clue.text: Repeat reasonable score? Nonsense

parts.note: par is the expected, reasonable score in golf
rot is nonsense, rubbish talk

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a fair mark should be repeated, then dismisses the idea as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot is to echo words mechanically, the way the talking bird does.

clue.text: I engaged in sleep after upturn in discomfort

indicators.note: the letter I is engaged, held, within the other letters
in a down clue an upturn turns the word for sleep upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

explanation.surface: Someone woke after a restless night of tossing and turning, and feels unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upturn' turns NAP into PAN, and 'engaged in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain and discomfort are near synonyms for physical suffering or unease.

clue.text: Temper one shows amongst American university crowd

indicators.note: the letter for one sits among the other letters

parts.note: MIT is the Massachusetts Institute of Technology
a gate is the number of spectators attending a sports match
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A student shows a bad temper in front of a crowd at an American campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' looks like a noun for anger, but it is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To temper something is to soften or lessen its severity, which is what mitigating does.

clue.text: Makes a loud sound — a good pair of lungs?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the verb for shouting or roaring
second meaning: informal for the lungs, a pair of air pumps

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful sense: lungs pump air like the fireside device.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means roars, and the noun names an air pump, used jokingly for a person's lungs.

clue.text: Composer giving you a lot of help?

indicators.note: a lot of means most but not all of the word help: three of its four letters

parts.note: those letters together make three quarters of this word, all but its P

explanation.surface: A musician is praised for being so supportive.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the composer's name as H AND EL; put together they spell most of HELP, missing only the P.
explanation.definitionFit: George Frideric Handel was the German-British baroque musician who wrote Messiah.

clue.text: One measuring concentration disturbed irate medic

indicators.note: disturbed letters are thrown into disorder, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor gets cross while someone keeps measuring how focused they are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concentration' suggests mental focus, but here it is the strength of an acid.
explanation.definitionFit: An acidimeter is an instrument for gauging the strength of acid in a solution.

clue.text: Resent move coming about for one Republican

indicators.note: the word for move comes around, surrounding the other letters

parts.note: to budge is to move slightly
EG, for example, is the same as 'for one'

explanation.surface: Someone resents a political move that has come about to benefit a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: To begrudge is to feel envious or grudging about something, the same as resenting it.

clue.text: A day in European city (Spain) — bliss

indicators.note: a day is put in the city's name

parts.note: Paris is the French capital
E is Spain's international vehicle registration code

explanation.surface: A traveller enjoys a blissful day in a European city before moving on to Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a state of perfect happiness, the same as bliss.

clue.text: Support about to be withdrawn for Olympic sportsperson

parts.note: an arch is a structural support

indicators.note: withdrawn, drawn back, so the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Backing for an athlete is about to be pulled.
explanation.definitionFit: Archery is an Olympic event, so an archer competes as an Olympic athlete.

clue.text: Determined club gets passed on to descendants

parts.note: an iron is a type of golf club
willed means bequeathed in a will to heirs

explanation.surface: A resolute golfer's club is bequeathed to their heirs.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone iron-willed has an unbending resolve, so is strongly resolute.

clue.text: Serious passion seen in pursuit of daughter

indicators.note: the word for passion follows, chasing after the daughter's letter

parts.note: ire is anger, a strong passion

explanation.surface: A furious parent chases their daughter in a serious mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Dire means grave or dreadful, which is a strong sense of serious.

clue.text: Star girl recalled dance performances (not debut)

indicators.note: called back, so the remaining letters are read backwards
the first letter, the debut, of the word for dance performances is dropped

parts.note: ballets are dance performances

explanation.surface: A young dancer remembers ballet shows other than her first one.
explanation.walkthrough: BALLETS without its first letter is ALLETS, which 'recalled' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: Stella is a girl's name that is Latin for star.

clue.text: Smart cars, large? Use Minis when travelling round Ohio

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round the letter for Ohio
letters that travel move about, so these are rearranged

parts.note: O is a recognised abbreviation for the US state of Ohio

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether big posh cars would be better than Minis for a road trip in Ohio.
explanation.walkthrough: Minis are small British cars; O for Ohio is a dictionary abbreviation, less familiar than OH.
explanation.definitionFit: Limousines are large luxurious chauffeured vehicles, the epitome of elegant motors.

clue.text: Craftsmanlike film director all but crazy inside

indicators.note: the word for crazy goes inside the shortened name
all but the last letter of the director's name is used

parts.note: Orson Welles directed Citizen Kane
mad means crazy

explanation.surface: A film director is praised for his craft despite being almost mad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all but' leaves WELLE, and 'inside' puts MAD within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-made work is skilfully constructed, the quality of a good artisan.

clue.text: Young female star backed accepting woman's title

indicators.note: the reversed word takes the title inside it
backed, moved back, so the word for star is read in reverse

parts.note: the lead is the star of a show
Ms is a title for a woman

explanation.surface: A young actress, a lead in a show, is given a woman's title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns LEAD into DAEL, which then accepts MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Damsel is an old word for a young unmarried woman or maiden.

clue.text: Idle hero of children's books?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... is to be idle
second meaning: Doctor ..., Hugh Lofting's character who talks to animals

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the answer splits into DO LITTLE, meaning to be lazy.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means being lazy, and the surname belongs to Lofting's animal-talking doctor.

clue.text: Web story not about to annoy

parts.note: a net is a web, a mesh

indicators.note: not signals the letter for about is left out

parts.note: a tale is a story
A is an abbreviation for about, approximately

explanation.surface: An online account that is not about anything is merely irritating.
explanation.definitionFit: To nettle someone is to irritate or provoke them, like the stinging plant.

clue.text: Writers in wartime possibly being censored badly

indicators.note: badly arranged letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Wartime letters writers sent home were heavily censored by the military.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' suggests authors; these are people writing messages in code.
explanation.definitionFit: Encoders put messages into cipher, a job done for secret military signals, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: No good in upper-class blade

indicators.note: no good means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: a cut-glass accent is a refined, upper-class one

explanation.surface: A posh weapon is judged to be of no use.
explanation.walkthrough: A cut-glass accent is the crisp speech of the British upper classes.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword with a broad blade, used by sailors and pirates.

clue.text: Nothing observed in outrageous clue, USA detective having no competence

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is seen inside the rearranged letters
an outrageous version of these letters is wildly rearranged

parts.note: O is the zero digit, nothing

explanation.surface: An American detective finds nothing in a ridiculous clue and is shown to be useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inspector Clouseau of the Pink Panther films is a famously bungling, incompetent sleuth.

clue.text: Noticed energy peaked, with a thousand running out

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

indicators.note: the thousand runs out, leaving the word for peaked

parts.note: spiked means peaked sharply
K stands for a thousand

explanation.surface: Someone observed their energy surge and then fall as a thousand people ran out.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to catch sight of, so espied means spotted.

clue.text: Ace, 22, seen around air aces with quantity of drink

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are seen surrounding the force's letters
22 is the answer to 22 down, flying, a word suggesting the letters of ace are sent flying into disorder

parts.note: the RAF, Royal Air Force, is home to flying aces

explanation.surface: A flying ace is spotted among other air aces, drink in hand.
explanation.walkthrough: The number 22 stands for that clue's answer, FLYING, which works here as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A carafe is a glass jug of wine or water, the amount served in one.

clue.text: Very brief affair around end of February

indicators.note: the word for affair goes around that letter

parts.note: a fling is a brief affair

indicators.note: the last letter of February

explanation.surface: A short romance came to an end at the close of February.
explanation.definitionFit: A flying visit is a hurried one, so the word means very quick or short.

clue.text: Quite complex, without question, but not much of a case

indicators.note: complex means intricate, so these letters are rearranged
the letter for question is taken away from the fodder

explanation.surface: A lawyer finds the matter rather complicated, but, without doubt, a weak case.
explanation.walkthrough: QUITE without Q leaves UITE, and 'complex' rearranges it.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental container for needles and sewing items.

clue.text: College cat lady unfortunately missing one with extra toes

parts.note: poly is short for polytechnic, a kind of college

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement of letters is a jumbled one
one letter for one is left out of the fodder

parts.note: A is one, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: A college's cat lady has an extra-toed cat, sadly missing one.
explanation.walkthrough: CATLADY minus A rearranged gives DACTYL. A polydactyl cat has extra toes.
explanation.definitionFit: Polydactyl describes an animal or person having more than the usual number of digits.

clue.text: Champion bridge team to ruminate?

parts.note: East and West form a partnership in bridge

explanation.surface: A winning bridge pair is asked to think things over.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows ruminate by chewing the cud, and to chew over something is to ponder it.

clue.text: Record keeper rubbed out cut by day before feast

indicators.note: the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: to rub out is slang for to kill, and slew means killed
an eve is the day before a festival

explanation.surface: A record-keeper is killed off the day before a feast.
explanation.definitionFit: An LP is kept in a cardboard sleeve, the protective cover for a vinyl disc.

clue.text: Irishman accepting quantity of work required by tense officer

indicators.note: the tense letter is placed after, as what the rest needs
the Irish name accepts the unit inside it

parts.note: Sean is an Irish male name
an erg is a unit of work in physics
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: An Irishman takes on work demanded by a stressed officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned army rank or a police rank.
